name: OpenBase SQL
tagline: NeXTSTEP-born relational server popular with WebObjects and Mac developers; the company is gone.
description: OpenBase SQL was a commercial relational database server from OpenBase International, started around 1991 on NeXTSTEP/OpenStep and later sold mainly to Mac OS X developers, with Linux support and admin tools for Mac, Windows and Linux. It combined a SQL engine with stored procedures, triggers, journaling for fault tolerance, synchronization between servers, incremental backups, a REST XML/JSON server and the OpenBase Manager GUI. Apple used it in its WebObjects tutorial demos, which won it a loyal following among WebObjects shops. The last major release, OpenBase 12 in July 2012, added 64-bit support for Mac OS X 10.6–10.8; the company's site went dark around 2020 and the product is no longer sold, so PostgreSQL is the usual migration target.
statusNote: OpenBase International's site closed around 2020 and the product is no longer sold; last major release OpenBase 12 (2012). Migrate to PostgreSQL.
strengths: Tight integration with Apple's WebObjects and Mac development tools
Easy administration through the OpenBase Manager GUI
weaknesses: Vendor gone; no updates since the early 2010s
useCases: Migrating legacy WebObjects or Mac business apps
